label: cor:ftc_eval
title: Evaluation of integrals via antiderivatives
statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$ and let $F$ be an antiderivative of $f$ on $(\min(a,b), \max(a,b))$ that is continuous on $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$. Then
    \[
      \int_a^b f(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a).
    \]
proof: By Lemma~\ref{lem:integral_is_antiderivative}, the function $G(u) = \int_a^u f(t)\,dt$ is an antiderivative of $f$ on the interior. By Lemma~\ref{lem:antiderivatives_diff_constant}, $F - G$ is constant on $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$, so $F(b) - G(b) = F(a) - G(a)$, which gives $G(b) - G(a) = F(b) - F(a)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:integral_base_zero}, $G(a) = \int_a^a f = 0$, so $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx = G(b) = G(b) - G(a) = F(b) - F(a)$.
